rows.text: This deck does not stop anyone from playing Magic. It charges them for it. Every card is a tax on an action an opponent has to take anyway — casting a spell, tapping a land, drawing a card — and the damage multipliers turn those small taxes into lethal ones. The pilot's job is to deploy the punishers, then STOP casting spells, because most of these effects are symmetrical and you are the only player who can choose to sit still.

rows.name: Kaervek the Merciless
rows.text: every spell an opponent casts deals its mana value to any target of your choice. Point it at faces, or use it as free removal on their creatures.

rows.name: Harmonic Prodigy
rows.text: Kaervek is a Shaman, so his trigger fires TWICE. Two mana, and it doubles the single biggest damage source in the deck.

rows.name: Lightning Greaves
rows.text: seven mana is a lot to lose to a removal spell. Shroud, and haste so he blocks or attacks immediately.

rows.name: Swiftfoot Boots
rows.text: hexproof and haste when you need to target him.

rows.name: Mithril Coat
rows.text: flash, indestructible, and it attaches itself to a legendary creature the moment it lands. Hold it as a counterspell for removal.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free, and it turns their removal spell into your removal spell.

rows.name: Painful Quandary
rows.text: five life or a card, on EVERY spell. The single most punishing card in the deck.

rows.name: Spellshock
rows.text: two damage per spell, for three mana.

rows.name: Pyrostatic Pillar
rows.text: two damage on every cheap spell — which is most of what a Commander table casts.

rows.name: Rug of Smothering
rows.text: one life per spell they have cast this turn, so it scales with combo turns.

rows.name: Magebane Lizard
rows.text: the same escalation aimed at noncreature spells.

rows.name: Adrenaline Jockey
rows.text: four damage to anyone casting a spell on someone else's turn. It makes instant-speed interaction cost four life.

rows.name: Gleeful Arsonist
rows.text: damage equal to its power on every noncreature spell, and undying means it comes back bigger.

rows.name: The Frightful Four
rows.text: their first noncreature spell each turn costs them its mana value in life.

rows.name: The Lord of Pain
rows.text: the first spell each turn deals its mana value to a player of your choosing — and it turns off their lifegain.

rows.name: Roiling Vortex
rows.text: a point per upkeep, no lifegain, and FIVE damage to anyone casting something for free. It blanks Force of Will, evoked Elementals and ritual-free combo turns.

rows.name: Harsh Mentor
rows.text: two damage for every nonmana activated ability they use.

guide.title: Taxing the rest of their turn

rows.name: Manabarbs
rows.text: a damage for every land tapped, by anyone. This is the card that ends games — and the one you must deploy last, because it hits you too.

rows.name: Ankh of Mishra
rows.text: two damage per land that enters. Brutal against ramp decks and fetchlands.

rows.name: Burning Earth
rows.text: a damage per nonbasic tapped. Be honest about this one: your own mana base is largely nonbasic, so it hurts you as well. Play it against a greedy multicolour table and not against a mono-coloured one.

rows.name: Spiteful Visions
rows.text: everyone draws an extra card and takes a damage per draw. You have the life total and the payoffs to win that race.

rows.name: Stormfist Crusader
rows.text: everyone draws and loses one every upkeep.

rows.name: Razorkin Needlehead
rows.text: a damage for every card they draw.

rows.name: Orcish Bowmasters
rows.text: flash, and it punishes every extra draw at the table while building an Army.

rows.name: Sheoldred, the Apocalypse
rows.text: two life for every card you draw, two lost for every card they draw. With Spiteful Visions out it is a four-point swing per turn cycle.

rows.name: Mogis, God of Slaughter
rows.text: two damage or a creature, from every opponent, every turn, on an indestructible body.

rows.name: Rampaging Ferocidon
rows.text: no lifegain for anyone, and a damage per creature they play.
This is where the deck turns a two-damage ping into a lethal one. The multipliers stack.

rows.name: Ojer Axonil, Deepest Might
rows.text: any red source you control dealing noncombat damage below its power deals FOUR instead. Pyrostatic Pillar's two becomes four; Magebane Lizard's one becomes four; Spellshock's two becomes four.

cards.name: Ojer Axonil, Deepest Might // Temple of Power

rows.name: Solphim, Mayhem Dominus
rows.text: doubles all noncombat damage you deal to opponents. Four becomes eight.

rows.name: Fiery Emancipation
rows.text: triples it. Eight becomes twenty-four, per spell they cast.

rows.name: Obosh, the Preypiercer
rows.text: doubles damage from your odd-mana-value sources, and Kaervek is mana value seven. He is NOT a legal companion for this deck — several cards here have even mana values — so treat him as a maindeck damage doubler.

rows.name: Basilisk Collar
rows.text: deathtouch and lifelink on any pinger. On Kaervek's trigger source it turns every spell they cast into a dead creature.

rows.name: Exquisite Blood
rows.text: you gain every point of life this deck drains. It is what lets you play Manabarbs and Spiteful Visions without losing the race.

rows.name: Deadly Rollick
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Feed the Swarm
rows.text: the only clean enchantment answer in these colours.

rows.name: Chaos Warp
rows.text: for the enchantment or planeswalker you cannot otherwise touch.

rows.name: Rakdos Charm
rows.text: graveyard hate, an artifact, or a symmetric ping that finishes a token board.

rows.name: Blasphemous Act
rows.text: cheap, and this deck's threats are mostly enchantments that survive it.

rows.name: Cursed Mirror
rows.text: a copy of the best creature on the board with haste, and a mana rock afterwards.

rows.name: Sol Ring
rows.text: turn-one acceleration toward a turn-four commander.

rows.name: Dark Ritual
rows.text: three black on turn one.

rows.name: Seething Song
rows.text: five red for three, which is how a seven-drop lands early.

rows.name: Mana Geyser
rows.text: red mana for every tapped land your opponents control. Cast it after they have all tapped out and it is often eight or more.

rows.name: Mana Vault
rows.text: three mana now, on turn one.

rows.name: Thran Dynamo
rows.text: three more, reliably.

rows.name: Crypt Ghast
rows.text: doubles every Swamp and extorts on every spell you cast.

rows.name: Black Market Connections
rows.text: three effects a turn, paid in life you are gaining back from Exquisite Blood.

rows.name: Night's Whisper
rows.text: two cards for two mana.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep fast mana. This deck wants a turn-two or turn-three punisher and a turn-four or five Kaervek; Sol Ring, Dark Ritual and the Signets do that, and a hand of five-drops does not.

Deploy the symmetrical cards LAST. Manabarbs, Ankh of Mishra and Spiteful Visions hurt you too. Cast everything you need to cast first, then land them and sit back — you win the race precisely because you can stop playing and they cannot.
Kaervek's damage does not have to hit faces. Killing the mana dork or the combo piece with a triggered ability nobody can respond to is often worth more than three damage to a life total.

rows.name: Harmonic Prodigy
rows.text: find it. Two mana that doubles Kaervek is the biggest single upgrade in the deck. Read it carefully though — it only doubles triggered abilities of Shamans and Wizards, so it does nothing for Ojer Axonil, Solphim or the enchantments.
